item.title: Warhammer Tone Pro: The 1-5 system
item.description: Five tones, infinite possibilities – dive into the new paints.
item.content:encoded:
The in-store release of the new Warhammer Tone Pro range is only days away! We’re spending the next few days taking a look at the key features of the new paints, starting with the 1-5 system.

The range features 30 colours, with five tones in each, giving you 150 new paints to add to your painting toolbox. The tones for each colour are numbered from 1 to 5, where 1 is the darkest and 5 is the lightest, and you have a really nice value shift between each tone. In most of the colours, 3 is the midtone, giving you two paints to highlight and two paints to shade with.

That doesn’t mean you have to use 3 as your base colour though. If you want to emulate how the ’Eavy Metal team paint the Ultramarines, you should start with Ultramar 2, shade with 1, and highlight with 3, 4, & 5.

The 1-5 system makes it really easy to navigate the colours, but you can also mix-and-match across the colours. For example Ultramar Blue could work with Blue Gorkshroom and Craventhrone Cloak to open up even more options.

The Warhammer Tone Pro range will be available in-store from Saturday. Head down to your local store to get your hands on them:

item.title: Designers’ notes: creating the new Tomb Kings of Khemri miniatures
item.description: The Warhammer: The Old World team tells us about making the new models.
item.content:encoded:
The imminent release of the Tomb Kings of Khemri Host of Nehekhara Army Reinforcement Set represents a huge awakening of the undead. To find out more about these brand-new miniatures, we caught up with the studio’s own Liche Priests to learn about bringing them to unlife.

Christian: The Tomb Kings of Khemri are a staple of the World of Legend, representing not just an army of the dead in service to a foul Necromancer, but the vast hosts of the Land of the Dead. This once great civilisation was cast down and awakened into undeath centuries ago by the vengeful magic of the Great Necromancer himself, Nagash. Since that time, the dead have plagued the lands of the living, driven to make endless war by their wicked rulers.

Keith: Much of the original Tomb Kings range was made a long time ago, using very different technology to what we have today. The original Skeleton Warriors, for example, combined the basic Warhammer skeletons of the time with a Tomb Kings upgrade sprue. This worked very well, but when we knew we were going to revisit the range, we wanted to really lean into the unique look of the faction established in the incredible art created for the old Warhammer Fantasy Battle army books.

Ethan: We were all familiar with the Tomb Kings armies, not only from the miniatures, but also from the classic art, of which there was a lot, and all done by some very talented artists. They really captured the look and feel of the undead armies of Nehekhara, bringing them to life on the page in a way Nagash himself would surely be envious of! Much like the recent Royal Heralds and Liche Priests kits, we wanted to update the classic models and capture the true character of the Tomb Kings.

Dan: We were also mindful that Tomb Kings of Khemri armies can include lots of models, with units like Skeleton Warriors and Skeleton Archers, for example, often being fairly large. So we wanted to make the models easier to assemble and, if possible, reduce the amount of separate parts compared to the old kits. The new Skeleton Archers in particular feature as few as three or four parts per model, but there are a lot of models on each sprue, 18 in both of the infantry kits, and still with room for lots of basing details in the form of scarabs, scorpions, and the remnants of statues toppled long ago.

Christian: The obvious starting point for an army of Tomb Kings warriors is with human and horse skeletons, both of which we’ve endeavoured to make more detailed and anatomically correct. Throughout the range we added touches of individuality as well. Some have missing teeth or jaws, cracked or fractured skulls, and so on. But what they all have in common is a sense of purpose. The armies of the Tomb Kings aren’t mindless, shambling undead. They are possessed of a spark of intelligence, haunted by the memories of lives long ago in which they were professional soldiers. Although they now serve their masters in undeath, we wanted the discipline of the soldiers they once were to be apparent in the models.

Despite being no more than lightly armoured skeletons, the skeletal warriors of the Tomb Kings stand tall and proud, holding their shields and weapons with purpose; they don’t slouch or drag their weapons. There’s a sense of order and readiness for battle to them.

Dan: Speaking of armour, this was one of the areas in which we were able to make the most improvements. Apart from their headgear, the old models lacked armour. Inspired by their battlefield roles we wanted to correct this. The Skeleton Warriors wear similar armoured headdresses and carry the familiar tall, tower shields of the past, but also feature more in the way of Nehekharan armour upon their chests and around their waists. The Skeleton Archers, by contrast, are more lightly armoured, with scarfs hanging over their faces and time-worn cloth hanging from their torsos and waists.

Ethan: We kept that time-worn look throughout. With the chariots, for example, we were inspired by real-world examples of chariots from antiquity, the better to understand how they were built and, from surviving examples, how they decayed over time. To give the idea that the armies of the Tomb Kings have often lain dormant under the arid sands for centuries, there’s lots of wear and tear on the models, visible in their crumbling clothing and armour, or on the slowly decaying edges of their shields.

The chariots also feature lots of options to make them more individual, from different armoured plates that mount on their front to alternative decorations for the yokes, weapon options for the crew, and full command, allowing you to build a distinct champion, standard bearer, and musician.

Keith: One thing that really sets Old World units apart is their distinctive command groups. Standing in the centre of the front rank, standard bearers, musicians, and champions really add character, and the Tomb Kings have always featured very distinctive standards in particular, alongside some suitably archaic instruments. For the standards, we kept the iconic designs and explored the iconography of the many gods of ancient Nehekhara and how their worship could be portrayed. There are lots of skulls and scarabs, for example, as well as asps and scorpions. Combined with flat areas that create space for transfers, it’s easy to add lots of unique character to your units, representing the ancient city they originate from, or the gods they once worshipped.

Speaking of transfers, the new kits are the first Tomb Kings of Khemri units to include transfer sheets, which depict the Gods Ptra, Djaf, Sokth, Asaph, and Geheb, along with a wide range of hieroglyphs.

Christian: Alongside the archaic bronze weapons – the ornate spears and khopeshes, the recurved bows, or the axes and maces of unit champions – the overall effect is of an army from a different age, yet one that still looks like it belongs on the battlefields of the Old World thanks to its legacy. We look forward to seeing the implacable hosts of the Tomb Kings advancing across the battlefield soon, a classic Warhammer army risen from the dead to make war on the living once more!

Thanks, folks! Now, you’ve learnt the dark magics behind the new miniatures, you’ll be able to pre-order the Host of Nehekhara Army Reinforcement Set from Saturday. Join us later in the week when we’ll be delving into the rules from Arcane Journal – The River of Bones.

item.title: On Warhammer TV this week – Devastation and drybrushing
item.description: Enjoy lore, painting challenges, and episode two of Arkanaut.
item.content:encoded:
Episode two of the animated series Arkanaut lands on Warhammer TV on Friday! We’ll have more details on that and the official trailer on launch day, but here’s what else you can enjoy in the meantime.

Available Today: Loremasters – The Devastation of Tallarn

The once-verdant muster world of Tallarn, with its vast network of defensible tunnels, became a target of the Traitor forces during the Horus Heresy, reduced to a desolate wasteland by the Iron Warriors.

However, thanks to the aforementioned tunnels, and the supplies within them, the people of Tallarn were able to launch a counterattack against the sons of Perturabo. In this episode, learn about Tallarn’s bleak history, the bitter fight for the planet, and how it played host to some of the largest tank battles in history.

Available Tomorrow: Tale of Four Gamers – Incursion of War

The four contestants reach the 1,000-point milestone and are ready for battle once more in a series of Incursion-sized games with their fledgling Warhammer 40,000 armies. We hear from the warlords as they talk through their army lists, tactics and strategies, and lessons learned in victory and defeat.

Available on Thursday: Ultimate Paint-off – Drybrushes Only

Ultimate Paint-Off sees our trio of painters push themselves, and each other to the limit. 

Our contestants must paint the largest model ever seen on Ultimate Paint-off – a Chaos Dragon from Warhammer: The Old World! While they have the full Warhammer Tone Pro paint range at their disposal, they only have the new Warhammer Pro Tone dry brushes to apply it with.

If you’re inspired by the use of the new Tone Pro paints, don’t forget that they will be available in-store from Saturday!

Available on Friday: Arkanaut – Episode 2: Endrinfall

As mentioned, episode 2 of Arkanaut is out on Friday. Captain Orra and her crew have claimed their prize – a Stormcast soul – and now they must defend it! Come back on Friday for more behind-the-scenes details from episode 2.

Also available on Friday is the epic original score of the Horus Heresy animation Kill Lupercal – perfect for soundtracking your weekend’s activities. It joins a range of soundtracks from other Warhammer TV animations, including Aeronautica Imperialis, Adepta Sororitas: Penitence, and more.

This week’s episodes join an immense back catalogue of over 700 episodes of gaming shows, hobby guides, animations, and more. Your subscription also unlocks expanded features in the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar apps, access to years of lore books and magazines in the Warhammer Vault, automatic entry into regular competitions, and even a pair of special subscriber-only miniatures and the Warhammer Yearbook when you sign up for a whole year. You’ll also get 12 months for the price of nine when you sign up for an annual subscription.

item.title: New Battleforce boxes revealed for Warhammer 40,000
item.description: Easily start a new army or grow an existing one.
item.content:encoded:
Christmas is quickly approaching – see what Warhammer 40,000 Battleforce boxes you’ll be able to pick up this festive season.

Space Marines: Indomitus Task Force

  • Captain In Terminator Armour

  • Chaplain

  • Redemptor Dreadnought

  • 5 Terminators 

  • 5 Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs

  • 10 Intercessors

The Indomitus Task Force gives you a versatile core to base a Space Marines army around, and includes a little bit of everything Warhammer armies need – shooting, fighting, and durability.

Chaos Knights: Helhunt Lance

  • Knight Ruinator (can alternatively be built as Knight Abominant, Knight Rampager, or Knight Desecrator)

  • 4 War Dog Stalkers (can alternatively be built as War Dog Brigands or War Dog Karnivores)

Dominate the battlefield by sending your tough and terrifying Chaos Knight up the middle of the battlefield while nimble War Dogs snap at the flanks. Just make sure to protect your big guy, and you’ll be stomping corpse-worshippers in no time.

Orks: Armoured Blitzmob

  • Warboss In Mega Armour

  • Battlewagon (can alternatively be built as a Gunwagon)

  • Deff Dread 

  • 3 Meganobz

  • 10 Ork Boyz

Load your Meganobz and Warboss into a Gunwagon and blast them up the field in double-quick time, before unloading everything into your opponent’s face at point-blank range. Build it as a Battlewagon, and you can even fit all 10 of the Boyz in at the same time.

Space Wolves: Champions of Fenris

  • Logan Grimnar

  • Arjac Rockfist

  • 15 Wolf Guard Terminators

Unleash Fenris’ finest with a mass of powerful Wolf Guard Terminators, led by the Great Wolf himself and his personal champion. It’s a force as blunt and savage as the Space Wolves themselves, and a terrifying prospect for any enemy.

Blood Angels: Angelus Assault Force

  • Commander Dante 

  • Blood Angels Chaplain with Jump Pack

  • Death Company Brutalis Dreadnought

  • 3 Sanguinary Guard

  • 5 Death Company Marines with Jump Packs

  • Blood Angels Upgrade Frame

The Blood Angels love a thunderous flight into the thick of the melee, and the Angelus Assault Force gives you units you need to crash down on your foes. All of your infantry hurtle in from above, while the enemy is rightly distracted by a rampaging Brutalis Dreadnought rapidly charging towards them.

Chaos Space Marines: Cult of Destruction

  • Warpsmith

  • Defiler

  • Venomcrawler

  • 2 Obliterators

  • 5 Havocs

  • 3 Mutilators

Heavy weapons and hulking daemon engines are a particular favourite of the Iron Warriors, but you can use this Battleforce to represent any Chaos warband. After all, who in their right mind would turn down a Defiler, especially one flanked by some of the toughest and deadliest infantry this side of the Great Rift?

Necrons: Disciples of the Nekrosor

  • C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer

  • Nekrosor Ammentar

  • 3 Ophydian Destroyers

  • Canoptek Doomstalker

  • 10 Necron Warriors

  • 3 Canoptek Scarab Swarms

Nekrosor Ammentar and his collection of Nightbringer C’tan Shards made an incredible mess around Ultramar and now have their sights set on the rest of the galaxy. Two powerful centrepiece miniatures surrounded by some Necrons mainstays is ideal for reclaiming your lost empire.

If you fancy picking up one of these Battleforce boxes for yourself, or as a Christmas gift for your Warhammer-inclined friends or family, they’ll be available for pre-order soon. Keep checking in with us to be the first to learn exactly when. And stay tuned to find out what’s on offer for Warhammer Age of Sigmar and Warhammer: The Horus Heresy.

item.title: Designers’ notes: The River of Bones lore
item.description: The Warhammer: The Old World team tells us about the background for the latest supplement.
item.content:encoded:
With the new Tomb Kings of Khemri miniatures and accompanying Arcane Journal coming out soon, we sat down with the writers from the Warhammer: The Old World studio to learn about the background of the book and discover what Settra and his undead forces are up to now.

JTY: Arcane Journal – The River of Bones is a continuation of the story that has been unfolding since the release of Warhammer: The Old World, a story that sees the eternal king of Nehekhara, Settra the Imperishable, leading his undead legions against the armies of the Old World. Since the arrival of Settra’s forces upon the shores of the Border Princes, the region has been thrown into turmoil, and a great many factions have been drawn into the fighting.

Dave: At the end of Arcane Journal – The War of Settra’s Fury, the previous installment in this tale, we saw Settra himself pursue his enemies from the ruins of Matorea to the towering walls of Louen Keep in the foothills of the Vaults. Whilst the great king occupied himself with laying siege to the ancient fortress, he commanded his armies in the west, led by High Priest Ashurtak of the Mortuary Cult, to advance northwards, through the Vaults and into the south-eastern corner of Bretonnia, Settra’s true objective.

JTY: Following many battles against the defenders of the Vaults, and more than a little time spent in the exploration of ancient tombs and forgotten temples, Ashurtak led his armies down the Mondidier Pass and towards the outskirts of Athel Loren.

This is where we pick up the action again in Arcane Journal – The River of Bones, with High Priest Ashurtak advancing into the great forest in search of its secrets. And well he might, for his armies have suffered tremendous losses in their advance, and many of the Liche Priests tasked with animating the undead legions have been slain during the campaign. If Ashurtak can seize control of the forest and the magic that flows through it, he will be almost unstoppable as he advances into Bretonnia.

Dave: Unfortunately for Ashurtak, Athel Loren is not lacking in defenders, and no sooner do the undead pass beyond the towering waystones that mark the great forest’s perimeter than they find themselves assailed on all sides. Pressing onwards, the undead are eventually brought to battle upon the banks of the mysterious Crystal Mere.

JTY: Alongside this unfolding story, Arcane Journal – The River of Bones gives us the opportunity to explore more of the World of Legend’s history, in particular, the expansion of Nehekhara and the extent of the power and influence it once wielded. For those unaware, Nehekhara once spread from the heart of the southern deserts to the very edges of the lands today known as the Empire. In those ancient times, the religion and culture of Nehekhara spread with its armies, and when Khemri’s influence waned following the demise of Settra* and the Great Land’s borders contracted, the Nehekharans left behind many ancient outposts and burial sites, filled with the mortal remains of loyal soldiers.

Dave: It’s these forgotten complexes that Ashurtak has been exploring and plundering on his march through the Vaults, reclaiming forgotten knowledge from lost temples and awakening long-dead legions to bolster his ranks. But what even he perhaps doesn’t know is that such forgotten sites exist further afield still, just waiting to be rediscovered.

JTY: Should these ancient barrows be disturbed, there’s no telling what fate awaits the denizens of the Old World. The defenders of Athel Loren likely don’t realise it, but a lot rests on their ability to defeat High Priest Ashurtak at the Battle of Crystal Mere!

Thanks, folks! The new Arcane Journal and Tomb Kings of Khemri miniatures are available to pre-order from Saturday. Join us later in the week when we’ll be chatting with the miniatures designers, and learning more about the new rules in the book.

* Something he’s still angry about.

item.title: Sunday Preview – Tomb Kings rise again
item.description: See what’s coming up for pre-order next week.
item.content:encoded:
The undead of Nehekhara rise from their tombs next week, with a new skeletal legion for the Tomb Kings of Khemri, along with the latest Arcane Journal. And this year’s incarnation of Da Red Gobbo goes up for pre-order ahead of his traditional Christmas mayhem.

Warhammer: The Old World – Host of Nehekhara Army Reinforcement Set

Reinforce your risen legions with a box packed with revitalised skeleton units for Tomb Kings of Khemri armies, loaded with ancient Nehekharan details and equipment options. The Army Reinforcement Set includes:

36 Skeleton Warriors
36 Skeleton Archers
6 Skeleton Chariots

Each of the units have cosmetic options, making it easy to customise your miniatures, and they come with optional champions, musicians, and standard bearers. This boxed set is only available while stocks last.

Warhammer: The Old World – Arcane Journal: The River of Bones

Follow Settra the Imperishable’s unstoppable march towards Bretonnia, and the wrath his High Priest incites from the Wood Elves of Athel Loren after corrupting a vital water source. This supplement contains new Armies of Infamy for the Tomb Kings and Wood Elves, as well as rules for using Gargantuan Treemen in Wood Elves armies, expanded magic item options, and more.

Warhammer: The Old World – Tomb Kings Dice and Cards

You can also grab a set of 20 thematic dice cast in bone-white plastic with a Tomb Kings icon on the six face, and a set of 54 reference cards so you never have to go leafing through your books to remember magic items, army abilities, spells, incantations, and more. After all, why would you want to stop looking at your awesome new skeletons? The dice and cards are only available while stocks last.

Warhammer 40,000 – Da Red Gobbo

Get ready for the festive season with everybody’s favourite mayhem-causing present re-distributor. This year’s version of Da Red Gobbo rides into action atop his squigmobile and will be getting rules for Warhammer 40,000, Kill Team, and Blood Bowl in the Festive Activities Guide.* Da Red Gobbo makes a characterful addition to any collection.

Black Library – New Hardbacks

Fan-favourite novel Grey Knights by Ben Counter gets the special edition treatment, featuring red foil page edges and a red ribbon page marker accenting its unique, foil debossed cover, and an additional short story. Can a Justicar and his hand-picked daemonhunters defeat a mighty daemon prince returning after 1,000 years of banishment?

This special edition will be available while stocks last and will go on pre-order at 3pm UK time on 28 October 2026.

The Raptors Chapter pit their unique skills against a tendril of Hive Fleet Leviathan in William Crowe’s Raptors: War and Shadow, a ragtag band of Astra Militarum survivors desperately hold out against an oncoming Ork horde in Crucible of Fire by Tom R Pike, and long-suffering Ratlings are sent out to capture the notorious Gretchin revolutionary in Da Red Gobbo’s Reckoning by Callum Davis.

Black Library – New Paperbacks

Four books also get regular paperback releases next week. Armageddon: Season of Fire by Jude Reid follows three Imperial warriors as they battle for Armageddon. Rhuairidh James’s Death Rider finds a commissar in the unenviable position of trying to prevent a suicidal attack by Death Korps of Krieg forces, when retreat from a victorious T’au Empire would help save their strength for later campaigns.

Alpha Legion Harrowmaster Solomon Akurra faces dissent, feuds, and lurking Imperial Assassins in Ghost Legion by Mike Brooks, where the promise of a new world to base his fractious warband comes under threat from the vengeful Imperium. Finally, a compilation of stories from across the 41st Millennium makes for the perfect dip-in-dip-out read in Treachery Unbound, where almost every faction you could think of gets their moment in a grand anthology proving just how grim and dark the far future really is.

This week is a packed one on Warhammer TV. Loremasters explains how the once-lush, former paradise of Tallarn came to be the desert waste we know now. Tale of Four Gamers sees the contestants take to the field for their first 1,000 point games, and Ultimate Paint-off gets to grips with the new Warhammer Tone Pro paint range in a difficult drybrush-only challenge.

At the end of the week, the second episode of Arkanaut launches from its berth, and to cap it all off, you’ll be able to listen to the heart-pumping score from Kill Lupercal.

Here on Warhammer Community, we’ll be diving into The River of Bones, and taking another look at Tone Pro paints before they land on shelves next weekend. Oh, and there’s the small matter of tomorrow’s reveal – who’d like to see what this year’s Warhammer 40,000 Battleforce boxes have in them?

* Available soon from your local Warhammer store.

item.title: Arkanaut Episode 1 – Meet the Therodoson
item.description: Watch the new Warhammer TV animation now.
item.content:encoded:
The new Warhammer Age of Sigmar animation Arkanaut just launched on Warhammer TV. This three-part series, from the same team that made Sigmar’s Toll, promises a new perspective on the setting, as it follows a crew of down on their luck duardin seeking riches in the skies of the Mortal Realms. 

Check out the trailer, or better yet, if you’re a Warhammer+ subscriber, watch the first episode now.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

Arkanaut features, as you might imagine, a company of Arkanauts – a pioneering and entrepreneurial crew of Kharadron Overlords. This rugged band are led by the enterprising Captain Orra, accompanied by the grizzled navigator Frodrikk.

The other big feature of the show, and almost a character in its own right, is the ship itself.

The Therodoson

Many Arkanaut ships are made to standard patterns, but are subsequently improved upon by their crew, who treat the vessel as ship, home, transport, castle, and fire support. Frigates, even more so than the Gunhaulers of the Grundstok and the Ironclad flagships, are as diverse as the privateer Kharadron that call them home.

The Therodoson is a particularly fine example. Hailing from the port of Barak-Zilfin, a city renowned for the speed of its ships and the daring of its sailors, this once-proud ship, like its crew, has fallen on hard times, and is long overdue for a trip to the Endrin Dock.

There are a few things a long-bearded Kharadron fan might notice about the Therodoson.

The runic inscription on the hull of the skyvessel is unique to every ship. Kharadron runes trace their lineage to the ancient Khazalid empire. In this instance the runes on the side of the Therodoson read “fearless seeker of fate and fortune”.

The Therodoson also sports a heavy skyhook, and unlike the Frigate miniature, which has an enclosed gunner’s canopy, the Therodoson has a partly open hatch (similar to that on the Ironclad miniature). This sort of modification is typical of the kind of customisation an Arkanaut crew might make to their vessel.

Because of the nature of animation, we get to see some parts of the Frigate in more detail than even the original Citadel miniature. We particularly enjoyed the detailing around the helm. True to the miniature, but necessarily more detailed, it features wheels, dials, levers, and the critical aether-gold gauge.

In case you fancy painting up a Therodoson for yourself, here’s a crisply rendered look at its full colour scheme.

Watch episode one of Arkanaut now on Warhammer TV, and join us next week for episode two…

item.title: Chronicles of Ruin – The Weight of Remembrance
item.description: Enjoy free fiction for the Khazalite Holds.
item.content:encoded:
The Khazalite Holds Army Set goes on pre-order tomorrow. Learn more about the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar faction with this free short story.

She crouched to listen to the stones, and through their vibrations, the stones spoke back.

‘The troggoths are in the western gallery, Thrynn,’ Helgur said, standing and brushing herself down. Over her head soared an archway of immaculate stone: the boundary mark of Karak Vigg. Beyond that was the tunnel ceiling, glimmering faintly, arcing down towards the half-finished gate into the hold behind them. ‘On the move now, as you might imagine.’

‘How long until they reach us?’ Thrynn Bjarki was a mountain of cave-bear fur, polished gromril and the accoutrements of various clans and guilds – a figure carved, as if by the Maker himself, into a monument to Khazalite culture. Amidst it all was a face and eyes that were stern but not quite unkind. Helgur shrugged, remaining just on the right side of respectful, as she dusted off her hands and glanced along the gloom-gripped passage before them.

‘With the luck of the Whitebeard? Still not long. Especially if the alpha-beast is among them. Likely before Kyng Vargrimm and his reinforcements arrive.’

‘Time enough to burn out any last nerves with a drink, though.’ The interjection was vigorous, lit with an undercurrent of flame. Helgur and Bjarki turned and watched as a wildly mohicaned warrior clad in drake pelt and gold approached from the duardin throng gathered at the hold’s entrance behind them.

Considering she had scowled through every war council and Great Recitation, Volna grinned now. It was an unusual expression on the scarred face of Urgma-Grimnir’s daughter; then again, it was unusual on the face of any Fyreslayer. Volna wore her battle-lust openly, though, three tankards of frothing magmalt ale drawn from the kegs the duardin had brought with them clutched in her broad hands.

‘One for you too, our worthy Stonesmith.’ The Fyreslayer thrust the sloshing mug at Helgur, downing a great swill of ale and wiping her mouth on the back of her hand.

‘I’m no Stonesmith, Runedaughter.’ Helgur took a drink, but her voice was terse. ‘I’m no less a fighter than you, as were all my line. I just… hear the stones.’

‘I hear them too, lass. You know what they tell me?’ Volna’s cinderous eyes flashed. ‘They talk of death. They talk about righting one more wrong. They talk of opening throats and splitting bellies and cleansing the rock with trogg blood. You know about that, lass? You know about vengeance?’

‘Aye,’ Helgur spat, reaching to the pendant around her neck. Her father’s sharp rune-work bumped beneath her finger, as it had many times since she had recovered it from what remained of his pulverised body. ‘Aye, I know about that.’

‘Enough, both of you. Defending the karak is what matters.’ Bjarki downed his own ale and gestured with his hammer back along the tunnel, to where pillars and half-built arches marked the edge of the Khazalites’ reconstruction efforts. ‘Grimnir would have our wrath saved for our enemies.’

‘See to your own duties, Thrynn. We’ll mind the Burning Berserker’s legacy.’ A harsh, gruff laugh left Volna as she raised her tankard in acknowledgement. A breath later and she turned, scale-cloak swirling, to march back to her glowering kin and grunting droth-beast at the eastern edge of the throng.

‘Strange folk, those Grimmdron slayers,’ Helgur said once she was gone, head shaking.

‘They might say the same of you, given how easily they bait you,’ Bjarki said, hammer braced over a shoulder. ‘I know you’re eager, lass. Just don’t lose sight of what we’re fighting for.’ 

‘Remembrance is strength. Through honouring what has been, we craft what is yet to be.’

‘Quoting my own words back at me, eh?’ Bjarki chuckled. He shook his head, beard swaying and clan-totems clinking. ‘Ah, niece. Your father was the same when we were lads, but he learned wisdom. We don’t put such stock in remembrance just to kindle hate. We remember to remind ourselves what is at stake.’ 

‘I know, lord-uncle,’ Helgur grunted, head bowed but not quite chastised. ‘But since it was this sort of beast that took him from us, some grudgement might be excused.’

‘Grudgement, aye. But grudgement must serve a purpose. Left untended, it digs to unhappy delves,’ Bjarki said, his tone suddenly severe. It did not last long before he sighed and clapped Helgur on the shoulder. 

‘Go on, girl. Greet your mother for me should you see her.’

Helgur set off at a steady jog, braids jostling. She passed ranks of duardin preparing for battle, acknowledging some with nods or grunts. Clans of axe and hammer compared the craftsmanship of their weapons; gunners sat carving resonant glyphs upon their ammunition; Runewrights performed final checks on the arcane mechanisms of great Oathkeeper guns. 

Amongst the war throng stood the Gholems. Each warrior-monolith seemed to possess its own gravity. The Gazulite Gholems, clutching their two-handed hammers, stood apart, the duardin who huddled around them chanting in low, morbid tones. Passing them, Helgur headed for the gleam of gold banding that marked the Valayan Gholems and the shield-maids clustered around them. 

‘How was your uncle?’ It was still odd, seeing Imnod clad as a templar of the hearth-goddess. That said, Helgur had always thought her mother had a severe aspect, and the tight mail coif and ceremonial hair buns had not diminished that impression. Perhaps that was why the matrons of Valaya’s guardian-shrine had recruited her. The will of the ancestors, they had said. That the summons came hours before they were due to have laid Helgur’s father to rest could not be helped.

‘Resolute, mother,’ Helgur said. ‘I expected more…’

‘Fire?’ Imnod asked, eyebrow arched. ‘Every battle is an echo of another. Through those echoes, we recall the virtue of those who fought them, so we might honour them.’

‘Words of the hearth-guardian?’

‘Of my own, girl!’ Imnod’s laughter was brief. Soon her face grew firm, and she gestured back along the torch-lit underway. ‘Beyond this gate lie our forges, our hearths, our folk. Now these beasts come to reduce all that to rubble. Steel and courage will cast them back.’

‘So folk keep telling me,’ Helgur nodded. ‘But I would rather honour Thorgrim and keep my grudge burning hot.’

A deep, bass gurgling echoed from further down the passage. As a hush fell over the throng, there came a wave of stench. Warriors jostled into position, shields locking. Imnod disappeared back into the ranks of her closed order. Helgur took position in the back ranks of her own warrior band just in time for someone to raise the cry.

‘Troggoths!’

The host of horribles shambled from the gloom, knuckles dragging and mauls carving furrows. They were accelerating. From amongst the Khazalite lines, light flashed and arcane energy left its peculiar odour as cannon-tenders struck the runes of activation, seeing their machines belch obliterating shot. Gunners joined the salvo, bullets whistling into eyes and soft flesh. Volna’s blazing slayers were already in motion; the right flank of the throng had charged to smash into the troggoth mob’s own, incinerating beast-flesh as they went. And all the while, the rest of the warrior throng clanged weapons against shields like great echoing gongs, stomped their feet and began to chant.

‘Clan Valankrom, who burned the gruel-beasts from the pits of Angaraz and made Ayadah safe anew, we remember your courage!’

‘The clans of Hasgaard, who honoured Grimnir and stood firm against the hordes of the Troggoth King, we remember your ferocity!’

‘Valaya the Defender, who broke the Gargant’s Gate and saved the clans of Karak Mogram, we remember your fortitude!’

‘And we remember those murdered by beasts,’ Helgur murmured quietly, reaching up to her father’s charm, ‘in whose name I will slay a hundred.’

Many troggoths had been engaged by the Fyreslayers; as sparks flew from gold-inlaid weapons, Helgur saw Volna’s Magmadroth rear up and let loose a blazing flame-stream at the mammoth brute grappling with it. But the rest of the beasts remained a juddering avalanche, and now they hit home. The first rank of duardin were knocked sprawling by their momentum. Not so the second. At Bjarki’s bellowed insistence, they gritted teeth, dug in heels, bent backs and pushed. They strode back against the troggoths even as the dull beasts grunted, baffled at why these little things were not simply breaking. They cleaved bellies or pinned beasts in place as firepower ripped through them. 

Imnod’s henge of Valayans was with them, drawing the enemy’s rage onto themselves while their long halberds speared and sliced. Helgur, along with the other reserve warriors, was preparing to join the scrum when an unhealthy groaning echoed off the tunnel wall beside them. In that pain was a warning, one that raked along Helgur’s spine.

‘The alpha-beast,’ she whispered as she fruitlessly scanned the fighting. ‘Inghilde’s lantern, where’s the alpha?’ 

There was an explosion of stone, a rush of force. Helgur was knocked from her feet as masonry and rock spun; it was this that saved her, her kin instead pulped into smears. As she blinked through the grit-haze, the sight of something monstrous shouldering through the destruction saw her spit a curse. The troggoth chief’s body seethed with motion: scuttling creatures of the deep and dark. In each hand, it carried half of an immense ancestor statue ground down into a club. 

Helgur doubted it had meant to punch through as part of some coordinated flank attack. Likely it had just wandered into a different tunnel and heard the sound of their chanting on the other side of the wall. Those beady yellow eyes locked upon her. She reached for her father’s charm, hoping to draw some measure of fury from it. Her fingers found the rune etched there. It was then, only then, that she recognised the pattern.

In her grief, in her grudgement, Helgur had not looked too closely at the actual design. She had presumed it was a weapon-rune. It was not; it was galaz. ‘Precious’. 

The beast looked along the duardin passageway, drawn towards the reclaimed works of the Khazalites by the light. Few save Helgur stood in its path of demolition. And, to her own surprise, that realisation burned through thoughts of vengeance.

‘I remember you, father,’ Helgur whispered. ‘I remember what you died for. Remember me as I die for it too.’

Getting to her feet, she moved to charge. The troggoth bellowed, raising a makeshift bludgeon. It swung, and her world went black – because she had closed her eyes. But the eternal darkness that should have followed did not. Instead came the resonant clang of weapon against shield. 

The orestone at the heart of each of the Valayan Gholems glowed with pulsing blue light as they stomped between Helgur and the marauding titan. Furious at being denied an easy meal, the troggoth set its shoulders and barged into them. One toppled, still swinging as it fell. The rest stood firm as the deep and resonant songs of Imnod’s henge of warriors flowed over the melee. The Gholems bashed the beast with their shields, splitting its lumpen nose. One hacked off an ear before having its own head annihilated with a wild swing.

A spinning shard of stone cut open Helgur’s cheek, seeing her flinch. The Gholems, for all their heroism, were being broken open. But they had bought seconds – crucial, unbending seconds. Seconds enough for a horn-blast to ring and the torches back down the underway passage to glow bright. Feet stamped and shields clanged to the echo of chanting, this time with force enough to shake the mountain.

Even as the Gholems battered it, the troggoth turned, brow furrowed – just as a spear of hexagonal rock burst from the earth and punched through its gut like an ore-pressing piston. The beast howled, dazed, as something equally huge sailed along an undulating current of rock towards it. Surrounded now by the Gholems, Helgur joined the cheers as the throne-barge of Kyng Vargrimm crashed forth, the duardin lord slicing through the troggoth’s neck with one punishing axe-swing. 

Warriors parted before him as the Kyng rode into the fray, the broken stone left by the troggoth’s entrance curving like a tube-wave at the chanting of Vargrimm’s Stonesmiths. Lightning spat from the drake-headed prows of his vessel, adding their firepower to the roaring barrage the Oathkeepers fired in his honour. Fresh clan warriors marched behind him, banners flashing with the sigils of the hold. Even some of Volna’s kin came with them, magmic veins of power threading along muscles as they sang ur-songs of awakening and doom.

Whatever intellect the troggoths possessed was not enough to see them retreat in time. Little by little, the duardin spilled over them, and their weapon arms did not tire. Helgur saw Imnod atop a felled brute, expression unbending as she stabbed down into its gaping mouth while shielding a wounded clan warrior with her body. Panicked, heavy breaths finally escaped Helgur’s chest. She allowed herself to sit as her heart slowed its hammering. One hand still clutched her amulet. 

‘I did not slay a single one, father. Not a single one.’ As she spoke, Helgur felt herself smile. Her body slumped against the leg of a Gholem, the stone warrior having now returned to a motionless docility. She glanced back along the underway. The torches burned bright. The pillars remained uncracked. The artifice of the duardin was unmarred. And where there was artifice, there was life. That, at least, was what the stones said to her now.

‘But I remembered. Remembered that vengeance isn’t everything. That we’re here to build, not just to slay. Perhaps that’s a good start, aye?’

The Khazalite Holds launch their campaign to reclaim their former empire tomorrow when their new army set goes on pre-order. In the meantime, enjoy some free Fyreslayers fiction as you prepare to unleash the  Grimmdrom alongside the Kromdron.

item.title: Da Red Gobbo returns with a new festive miniature
item.description: Plus, there’s a new novel starring the galaxy’s greatest revolutionary gretchin.
item.content:encoded:
Da Red Gobbo is back with another festive miniature – and this time he’s got himself a Squigmobile. Just make sure you’re out of the way – we’re not convinced he knows how to stop!

Da Red Gobbo’s Squigmobile is a roaring, clanking contraption geared towards delivering presents at exceptionally high speed, which we dare say channels more than a few Wazdakka Gutsmek vibes. His long-suffering ‘elf’ assistant looks frankly miserable in the bomb-shaped sidecar – which honestly might just be a live bomb – but knowing what a jolly fellow Da Red Gobbo can be, he’s probably overreacting.

See, da Gobbo is a safety-conscious boss. He’s even wearing a helmet.*

This miniature will be available to pre-order soon, and if you want to use it in some fun casual games, make sure to grab this year’s Festive Activities Guide from your local Warhammer store in November. It contains Legends rules for Warhammer 40,000, Nemesis Operatives rules for Kill Team, and as unlikely as it sounds, Blood Bowl rules.

Alongside the Squigmobile, our favourite yuletide revolutionary stars in a brand-new novella from Chem Dog author Callum Davis – Da Red Gobbo’s Reckoning.

This raucous tale revolves around the ratling fixer Ector Flynn and his squad of snipers, who are sent into a snow-cloaked wasteland by choleric Catachan commanders to hunt Da Red Gobbo down. After months of being bullied and knocked around by the Jungle Fighters, Flynn’s team welcome the chance to finally prove their worth, but nothing goes to plan when Da Gobbo is involved and they may come back learning a little something about vengeance from their red-coated quarry.

Keep an eye on Warhammer Community to find out when you can pick up the new miniature and book. In the meantime, catch up with the rest of Da Red Gobbo’s adventures with Long Live Da Red Gobbo, Da Gobbo’s Demise, Da Gobbo’s Revenge, and Da Gobbo Rides again – all available via the Black Library app.

* Health and safety isn’t just for the Iron Warriors.

item.title: Khazalite Holds Clanshields Kit Focus
item.description: Get a closer look at the new duardin miniatures for Warhammer Age of Sigmar.
item.content:encoded:
The new Khazalite Holds Clanshields kit is packed with awesome build options, making it simple to customise your unit. Take a look at just how many ways you can put together the miniatures.

The 10 miniatures come with interchangeable shields – 10 with one rune so you can have a unified look, and the other 10 with different runes to mix it up.

The heads are also interchangeable and there are enough with beards that you can give them all a hirsute appearance if you like. 

Each Clanshield can be armed with a hammer or an axe – they have the same in-game profile as each other, and if the Kromdron can’t pick a favourite then you shouldn’t have to either.

The kit also includes parts to build an optional champion, standard bearer, and musician, all with more cosmetic options. The champion has a choice of two tactical rocks and three icon plates that they share with the standard bearer. Speaking of your banner waver, they have a choice of two standards, each with a choice of toppers, while the musician can choose from two different warhorns.

As well as being an incredibly flexible kit, the Clanshields are the backbone of Khazalite Holds armies. Their 3+ save makes them resilient and they get to add 1 to their wound rolls when they have any grudge marks.

These new miniatures will be available for the first time in the Khazalite Holds Army Set, which is available for pre-order from Saturday. The army set makes a complete Spearhead – Drakkblud’s Clanguard.

Led by Hjulda Drakkblud, the Clanshields are supported by an Oathkeeper Cannon – firing stone-carved ammunition – and three Gholems of Gazul, who can each have different runes on their hammers.

The Oathkeeper Cannon can alternatively be built as a Stonebreaker Mortar, and the Gholems of Gazul can alternatively be built as Gholems of Valaya. These additional build options aren’t included in the Spearhead assembly guide in the army set, but you can download for free now:

item.title: Mix your favourite duardin with Khazalite Holds Armies of Renown
item.description: New rules from the upcoming Warhammer Age of Sigmar battletome.
item.content:encoded:
Now that we know how our new Khazalite warriors hold fast to their grudges and pull power from their ancestral vows, it’s time to see how you can build fun and thematic armies that mix all kinds of duardin using three new Armies of Renown.

Valankrom’s War Throng

The first doubles down on the new Khazalite Holds miniatures by taking High Kyng Valankrom – on his epic War Throne – alongside kromdron units like Clanshields and Valayan Guardians, seasoned with plenty of rock hard Gholems. In Valankrom’s War Throng, your Gholems become immovable bodyguards for the High Kyng, while Valankrom judges enemy units to be wrongdoers who confer the effects of additional grudge marks on anyone who attacks them.

VALANKROM’S WAR THRONG

Once Per Turn (Army), End of Any Turn

THE AUDACITY!

Who dares attempt to lay a hand on our High Kyng?

Declare: Pick each enemy unit that used an ability that inflicted any damage on the friendly High Kyng Valankrom this turn to be the targets.

Effect: Each target is a wrongdoer for the rest of the battle.

VALANKROM’S WAR THRONG

Passive

REMEMBER THEIR PERFIDY

Retribution is long overdue, and it shall be meted out in earnest.

Effect: Friendly VALANKROM’S WAR THRONG units are treated as having 1 grudge mark while they are in combat with an enemy wrongdoer.

Most of the abilities conferred by this Army of Renown center around the High Kyng himself, so it’s a great way to get the most out of your jawdropping centrepiece miniature. You’ll want him in the thick of it too, as he’s as hard as nails and dishes out tons of damage between his relic hammer Bharadreng and the weapons of his Karak War Council.

Fyrd of Fyrepeak

If you’ve already got a sizable Fyreslayers army and want to head out and claim vengeance for the destruction of the magmaholds, the Fyrd of Fyrepeak gives you an outlet for your righteous rage. Generating grudge marks is as easy as slaying enemy units, so your Grimmdron only grow stronger as the game goes on, and if you’re confident a hero can take out a chosen enemy champion you can spread grudge marks across your entire army in one go with the Foeseeker heroic trait.

FYRD OF FYREPEAK

Passive

GRIMMDRON GRUDGES

The blood of the foe stokes the flames of vengeance in the Fyreslayers.

Effect: Each time a friendly FYRD OF FYREPEAK unit destroys an enemy unit, give that friendly unit 1 grudge mark.

FYRD OF FYREPEAK

Deployment Phase

FOESEEKER

There is one among the enemy whose transgressions against the Grimmdron are grave in the extreme. This Fyreslayer has sworn to have their head.

Declare: Pick an enemy HERO to be the nemesis for the rest of the battle. You can pick an enemy unit in reserve.

Effect: If the enemy nemesis is destroyed by this unit, after removing the destroyed unit from play, give each friendly FYRD OF FYREPEAK unit on the battlefield 1 grudge mark.

If this unit is within 12" of the enemy nemesis when it is destroyed but it did not destroy the enemy nemesis, after removing the destroyed unit from play, give each visible friendly FYRD OF FYREPEAK unit wholly within 12" of this unit 1 grudge mark.

They also get their own set of five once-per-battle abilities from the Fyreslayers’ Ur-gold runes. Each one confers a powerful bonus for the rest of the round, so if you need to make critical runs and charges, strike the Rune of Speed and re-roll them all.

FYRD OF FYREPEAK

Once Per Battle (Army), Any Hero Phase

FOESEEKER

This rune is commonly embedded in the legs of Fyreslayer warriors. When awakened, it sees them hurtle towards the enemy lines with fearsome swiftness.

Effect: You can only use this ability if you have not used any UR-GOLD RUNE abilities this battle round.

For the rest of the battle round, you can re-roll run rolls and charge rolls for friendly FYRD OF FYREPEAK units.

 KEYWORDS: UR-GOLD RUNE

Throngankor Alliance

Finally, call in your airborne cousins with the Throngankor Alliance, letting you combine Khazalite Holds and Kharadron Overlords units who defend each other to the death when fighting shoulder-to-shoulder. 

THRONGANKOR ALLIANCE

Once Per Turn (Army), Start of Battle Round

STONE AND SKY

When the duardin of karak and sky‑port unite, their alliance is strong indeed.

Declare: Pick a friendly non-HERO KHAZALITE HOLDS INFANTRY unit and a friendly non-HERO KHARADRON OVERLORDS INFANTRY unit that are within ½" of each other to be the targets.

Effect: For the rest of the battle round, while the targets are within ½" of each other:

  • The targets have the STONE AND SKY keyword.

  • Subtract 1 from wound rolls for attacks that target those friendly units.

These enterprising duardin work so well together that Khazalite units can even hitch a ride on the Kharadron skyvessels as they soar about the battlefield. Just imagine how surprised the enemy will be when they expect a bunch of Arkanauts to hop out of an incoming Frigate, only to have a reinforced brick of Valayan Guardians launch from the deck.

If you’d prefer to leverage the Kharadron Overlords’ superior shooting rather than get them stuck into close combat, you can use the Hammer and Anvil ability to have their fightier kin distract an ideal target. The ‘anvil’ engages the enemy in combat, only for the ‘hammer’ to score a bunch of critical hits when they open fire – pure teamwork in action.

THRONGANKOR ALLIANCE

Once Per Turn (Army), Reaction: You declared a Move ability for a friendly Skyvessel in your movement phase

TRANSPORT DUARDIN

The duardin take to the skies upon the deck of the Kharadron skyvessel.

Effect: Pick a number of THRONGANKOR ALLIANCE INFANTRY units up to that SKYVESSEL’s Transport Capacity (see its warscroll) that are wholly within 6" of it, visible to it and not in combat to be the targets. Units that have been transported this turn cannot be targets.

Remove the targets from the battlefield. After the SKYVESSEL ends its move, you must set up each target unit on the battlefield, wholly within 6" of that SKYVESSEL and not in combat. Those units have been transported. A unit cannot use CHARGE abilities if it was transported in the same turn.

THRONGANKOR ALLIANCE

Once Per Turn (Army), Your Shooting Phase

HAMMER AND ANVIL

The hammer shall crush that which lies between it and the anvil.

Declare: Pick a friendly non-STONE AND SKY THRONGANKOR ALLIANCE unit that is in combat to be the anvil. Then, pick an enemy unit in combat with the anvil to be the workpiece. Finally, pick a friendly THRONGANKOR ALLIANCE unit that is not in combat and does not have the same faction keyword (i.e. KHAZALITE HOLDS or KHARADRON OVERLORDS) as the anvil to be the hammer.

Effect: For the rest of the turn, the hammer’s ranged weapons have Crit (2 Hits) for shooting attacks that target the workpiece.

All of these new Armies of Renown come in the brand new Khazalite Holds battletome, and if you want to get your hands on it first, you’ll have your chance when the Army Set goes up for pre-order on Saturday. It’s a whole new faction coming to Warhammer Age of Sigmar – what are you waiting for?

item.title: More Khazalite Holds army rules revealed
item.description: Learn how the duardin swear Ancestral Vows to receive divine power in their new battletome.
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday, we took a look at how grudge marks work for the Khazalite Holds. Today, we’re learning about their other main battle trait – Ancestral Vows.

The Khazalite Holds place their faith in several Ancestor Gods, be it Valaya – warrior goddess, and stoic defender of hearth and hold – or their indomitable death god Gazul. So strong is their belief that they can invoke some of the powers of the gods in battle – there are five potent Ancestral Vows to pick from, but each can only be used once per game.*

The effects themselves are profound. We Honour Valaya is a powerful one-time ability that heals units and dishes out damage in equal measure, and it gets even stronger when invoked on Valayan Guardians.

BATTLE TRAITS

Once Per Battle (Army), Any Hero Phase

WE HONOUR VALAYA!

These duardin ask Valaya for the strength to strike down a foe and to stand resolute in the face of adversity.

Declare: Pick up to 3 friendly DUARDIN KHAZALITE HOLDS units in combat to be blessed by Valaya. Then, for each unit blessed by Valaya this turn, pick an enemy unit in combat with it to be its target.

Effect: Roll a D3 for each unit blessed by Valaya this turn. If that unit is VALAYAN, use a value of 3 instead. Inflict an amount of mortal damage on its target equal to the roll. Then, you can pick 1 of the following:

  • Heal (X) the unit blessed by Valaya, where X is equal to the value of the roll.

  • Return a number of slain models to the unit blessed by Valaya with a combined Health characteristic of up to the value of the roll.

You cannot use any other ANCESTRAL VOW abilities for the rest of the battle round.

KEYWORDS: ANCESTRAL VOW

The fallen Slayer god Grimnir still gets respect from the Khazalites – doubly so now that the Fyreslayers have moved in to escape their overrun magmaholds. His own Ancestral Vow, Grimnir’s Wrath Will Burn Bright!, is a brutal boost to your chosen units’ fighting prowess, and can turn the tide of a hard-fought battle in moments.

BATTLE TRAITS

Once Per Battle (Army), Any Hero Phase

GRIMNIR’S WRATH WILL BURN BRIGHT!

Roaring dedications to Grimnir, these warriors throw themselves into battle, their god’s fury coursing like magmalt ale through their veins.

Declare: Pick up to 3 friendly DUARDIN KHAZALITE HOLDS units to be the targets.

Effect: For the rest of the battle round:

  • Add 1 to wound rolls for the targets’ combat attacks.

  • If a target is GRIMMDRON INFANTRY, it has STRIKE-FIRST if it charged in the same turn.

You cannot use any other ANCESTRAL VOW abilities for the rest of the battle round.

KEYWORDS: ANCESTRAL VOW

There are three other Ancestral Vows to space out across your battle:

  • Inghilde, our Light in the Darkness – Use hidden tunnels to quickly traverse the battlefield.

  • By Grungni, Stand Firm! – Fortify your armour by remaining vigilant and not being suckered into charges.

  • Enlighten us with your Wisdom, Grombrindal – Cast spells and chant prayers more easily and resist their effects on your duardin.

As you might imagine, many of the Khazalite Holds infantry are built to make good use of these powerful bonuses – especially Inghilde’s ancestral vow. 

While Gholems can’t take advantage of Ancestral Vows, they provide some devastating close-combat support for the rest of your army. With their Gazulite great hammers and Armour-crushing Swings ability, the Gholems of Gazul can easily smash their way through enemy lines.

GHOLEMS OF GAZUL

MELEE WEAPONS

Atk

Hit

Wnd

Rnd

Dmg

Gazulite Great Hammer

3

4+

2+

2

3

Once Per Turn (Army), Any Combat Phase

ARMOUR-CRUSHING SWINGS

Even a glancing blow from a Gazulite hammer can ruin the target’s armour. The wise take pains to get out of the way, though at the expense of faltering in their own attacks.

Declare: Pick an enemy unit in combat with this unit to be the target.

Effect: Your opponent can pick whether the target will attempt to sidestep or not. If they do, subtract 1 from hit rolls for the target’s attacks for the rest of the turn. 

Then, roll a dice. Subtract 1 from the roll if the target attempted to sidestep. If the roll equals or exceeds the target’s Save characteristic, subtract 1 from save rolls for the target for the rest of the turn.

One of the keys to getting the most out of the Khazalite Holds is choosing the right Ancestral Vow at the right time. Then, if it all goes badly, you still have the army-wide passive ability Gazul, Remember the Fallen!, which adds 1 to the attack characteristics of the melee weapons of a duardin unit that has lost at least half of their models. 

The Khazalite Holds Army Set goes up for pre-order on Saturday. Come back later in the week when we’ll be looking at the three Armies of Renown in the battletome, including one that features a coalition of Khazalites and Kharadron Overlords.

* Also, only one per battle round in total. Don’t go dividing your ancestral attention now.

item.title: Khazalite Holds battle traits – Hand out some Grudges
item.description: New army rules from the upcoming Warhammer Age of Sigmar battletome.
item.content:encoded:
The Khazalite Holds have a new battle trait – grudge marks. It doesn’t take much to get one, and duardin don’t like leaving a grudge unanswered – learn how these new rules work.

Once the enemy has committed a slight against your duardin, you get to hand out grudge marks in accordance with their wonderfully named battle trait, Thorgrim’s Beard! There are Grudges to be Settled!

BATTLE TRAITS

Once Per Turn (Army), End of Any Turn

THORGRIM’S BEARD! THERE ARE GRUDGES TO BE SETTLED!

Every slight against these duardin will be remembered and returned with interest.

Effect: If your general was destroyed this turn, you can give up to 3 friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS units 1 grudge mark.

Otherwise, pick up to 3 of the following effects:

  • If any friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS units were destroyed this turn, give 1 grudge mark to a friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS unit.

  • If any friendly KROMDRON units are contesting an objective that is being contested by any enemy units, give 1 grudge mark to a friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS unit.

  • If any friendly GRIMMDRON units charged this turn, are in combat, have not been destroyed and did not destroy an enemy unit this turn, give 1 grudge mark to a friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS unit.

  • If any damage points were allocated to your general this turn, give 1 grudge mark to a friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS unit that is not your general.

This can come from losing a Khazalite Holds unit to enemy attacks, contesting an objective that’s rightfully yours, or refusing to die properly when attacked by the Grimmdron. The passive battle trait Reclaim the Karaks can also dole out some grudges against foes who set foot on your home ground, but it’s a double-edged sword that’ll remove those marks again should your units shame themselves by using the Retreat ability.

Finally, a Hero’s keen eye for minor grievances can also Let It Be Known that their troops have missed a grudge they really should be grumbling about.

These duardin have sworn to take back their lands from those who would defile them.

Effect: Immediately after your opponent gains control of an objective within your territory, you can give 1 grudge mark to a friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS unit.

Each time a friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS unit uses the ‘Retreat’ ability, after that ability has been resolved, you must remove 1 grudge mark from that unit (if it has one).

BATTLE TRAITS

LET IT BE KNOWN!

With rousing indignation, a hero of the hold reminds their kinfolk of the misdeeds committed by their foes.

Declare: Pick a friendly KHAZALITE HOLDS HERO to use this ability, then pick a visible friendly non‑HERO KHAZALITE HOLDS unit wholly within 12" of that HERO to be the target.

Effect: Until the start of your next turn, the target has 1 additional grudge mark.

Each duardin deals with their grudges differently, and their unit warscroll will tell you what bonuses they get for having a grudge mark. For example, Thrynns have their Steadfast Retribution ability, which gives them a boost to their Attacks for every friendly unit with a grudge mark nearby.

Put your Thrynn near some particularly powerful melee units such as Valayan Guardians with Runic Halberds and Hearthguard Berzerkers when they have a grudge mark and watch them smash through enemy lines with their extra attacks.

Clangunners come in two variants, with thrundok rifles or thrundrin shotcannons, and each gains a different effect from their grudge mark. Not all grudge mark abilities are offensive in nature. Unsurprisingly given their tempers, the Fyreslayers get plenty of use out of grudge marks too, like the Auric Runesmiter who gets a nice and simple bonus to his chanting rolls. The Khazalite Holds have a new prayer lore to get the most out of this bonus, and it channels Ancestor God Recitations – a Priest invoking a Recitation to Grimnir will lash their target with mortal damage when they try to act in their turn, while Recitations to Valaya and Gazul have similarly potent effects.

item.title: Only in Death: 40,000 Ways to Die – New Animation
item.content:encoded:
It might sound great to be a genetically enhanced superhuman killing machine, but the life of a Space Marine is far from sunshine and roses. In fact, what you thought was sunshine is just as likely to be the flash of an Aeldari starcannon 0.1 seconds before it utterly vaporises you.

With their new Codex on the way, we thought it high time we took a look at the reality of life as a Space Marine in the 41st Millennium, through the medium of endearing cartoon-animated Intercessors being mercilessly dismembered.

Enjoy!

item.title: The Art of Warhammer – Terra and the Custodes
item.description: Behold the golden heart of Humanity and the bodyguards of the Emperor.
item.content:encoded:
Our ongoing art series heads to the cradle of the Imperium with some images of Holy Terra and its towering golden protectors – the Adeptus Custodes. Few images of the God-Emperor’s seat of power are seen in the far reaches of the galaxy, so enjoy your views of this wondrous place.

Our art series will return soon. You can prepare to take your own place on the parapets of the Throneworld when Codex: Adeptus Custodes goes up for pre-order tomorrow.

item.title: Space Marine 2 gets a massive anniversary update
item.description: Celebrate the start of Year 3 with a new weapon and play as Chaos Space Marines in Siege Mode.
item.content:encoded:
A new update is out today for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2, with a new weapon, new chances to play as dastardly heretics, and new challenges for the most daring players.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

Let’s start with the new Champion pack. The Space Wolves send one of their best with an incredible new armour set based on the Wolf Guard Battle Leader, complete with a round Fenrisian storm shield so you can use it with the Bulwark class. 

This modified MkX Tacticus suit is covered in furs and fangs befitting one of the Chapter’s most storied veterans.

But wait, what’s that he’s holding up there? From today, players can bash xenos skulls in and sunder Rubric power armour with a mighty one-handed thunder hammer! This brutal weapon is faster than the two-handed variant and can charge up to deal rippling area-of-effect blows, making it a great option for all kinds of foes.

Players using the Tactical, Assault, Bulwark, and Techmarines classes can all take the one-handed thunder hammer into battle, and there’s even a powerful Heroic version – the Power Maul.

These come alongside top-end additions for the power axe, auto bolt rifle, and five new cosmetic items bought with Accolades, including a fancy shoulderpad for the Black Templars and an Iron Halo.

The Tactical class is getting a top-to-bottom rework in this patch, renovating large swathes of its skill tree to offer more varied and interesting build options. It will also be getting access to the one-handed thunder hammer, the power axe, and the power sword, though with any of these powerful melee options equipped, you’ll lose access to your primary weapon.

So what if you want to take a bolt rifle and a power axe? There’s actually a Signature Perk for that – replacing the old Signal Jammer, you’ll now be able to choose an option that lets you take the regular, humble bolt rifle in your secondary weapon slot, with progression shared with its normal primary slot version. Tactical specialists really are the most versatile Space Marines in the squad.

If you’re looking for more of a challenge to test out the new skills, or simply enjoy running through Operations as close to the wire as possible, try out the new Crucible mode to earn Crucible XP. By talking to the Company Chaplain on board the battle barge you can activate Penances – personal debuffs that make your run harder – and completing missions with them active will put you on track to earning a set of Lamenters armour pieces.

Alongside the Space Wolves Champion Pack, the mysterious Exorcists Chapter also gets a Cosmetic Pack added to the Season Pass. This set of stylised armour pieces includes one Helmet, two Left and Right Pauldrons, two Left and Right Gauntlets, and one Breastplate from everyone’s favourite daemon-hunting Successor Chapter, covered in purity seals and arcane script.  The Space Wolves Champion pack and Exorcists Chapter Pack are available to buy individually and also as part of Season Pass 3, whilst everything else included in the update is free. 

Fancy getting a bit traitorous? A new spin on the wave-based Siege mode lets you step into the boots of a Chaos Space Marine to slaughter Tyranids, Imperial Guardsmen, and even loyalist Space Marines as you fight for dominion over Avarax. The new mode will initially include two sectors, with a third planned for a later release.

On top of all of this, we’ve still got room for a few more free additions. Heroic weapon variants of the power axe, one-handed thunder hammer, and auto bolt rifle will be added to the armoury, along with five new armour pieces and an expansion of the wargear sharing system. A third slot will open up to be used with capes, tabards, and iron halos, while some new items for Vanguard, Heavy, and Assault classes can be unlocked with new Ordeals.

This is only the first big update coming over the next 12 months, and the Year 3 battle plan is stacked with enough new content to fill a battle barge, from new weapons and new operations to an entirely new class – the Apothecary! Check out our first look at the schedule.

And that just about covers it! Head into Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 now to try out the new update, and get yourself prepared for Year 3.
